# Supporting-facet transport: exact intrinsic reduction and incoming mass
polytopal-attainment assertion, no assumed regularization of an attained
minimum, and no conclusion of OC from these identities.

The existing candidate 22fb802a1dc82eb3 retains
transport-induced target ownership fractions. The result here identifies
exactly when the *full unweighted* facet restriction is a lower-dimensional
transport problem, gives the lattice and metric normalization explicitly,
and proves by a positive-density example that the required balance need
not hold even on either facet of one fixed continuous-normal sector.

## 1. Data and the exact incoming-mass identity

Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\), \(d\ge1\), be a
full-dimensional compact polytope. Assume every nonempty integer fiber
\(K_p\) has positive \(d\)-dimensional volume. Let \(\eta\) be the
sum of the actual \((d-1)\)-dimensional fiber boundary measures,
with their almost-everywhere unique outward continuous normal marked.
For \(d=1\) this means counting the two endpoints of each interval.

Let \(\nu\ll\eta\) be finite and let \(\Pi\) be a physical martingale
coupling from \(\nu\) to \(\eta\), preserving the marked continuous
normal. Thus its source and target physical coordinates \(w,w'\)
satisfy \(E[w'\mid w,u]=w\). No cap-minimality condition is assumed.

Fix a nonvertical ambient supporting facet
\[
 F=C\cap\{a\cdot z+u\cdot x=b\},\qquad |u|=1,              \tag{1}
\]
where \(a\cdot z+u\cdot x\le b\) on \(C\). Physical restrictions
below include all marks at the selected physical points.

**Facet incoming-mass lemma.** Every source row at \(F\) stays in
\(F\). If \(\eta_F^0\) is the target law of those source rows, then
\[
 \eta_F^0\le\eta|_F,\qquad
 \zeta_F:=\eta|_F-\eta_F^0
   =(\text{target projection})_\#
       \bigl(\Pi|_{\{w\notin F,\ w'\in F\}}\bigr).          \tag{2}
\]
In particular
\[
 L_F:=\eta(F)-\nu(F)
    =\zeta_F(F)
    =\Pi\{w\notin F,\ w'\in F\}\ge0.                     \tag{3}
\]
The restriction to source rows in \(F\) couples \(\nu|_F\) to the
*entire* \(\eta|_F\) if and only if \(L_F=0\). Whether or not
this holds, adding the diagonal coupling of \(\zeta_F\) yields
\[
 \nu|_F+\zeta_F\ \le_{\rm cx}\ \eta|_F                    \tag{4}
\]
as measures in the affine hyperplane of \(F\).

**Proof.** The nonnegative variable
\(b-a\cdot z'-u\cdot x'\) has conditional mean zero whenever the
source lies in \(F\); hence it vanishes in those rows. Restricting
the target marginal according to whether the source is in \(F\)
gives (2). Taking masses gives (3). Zero mass of a nonnegative
measure is equivalent to its vanishing, proving the criterion.
The restricted rows retain their source barycenters. A diagonal
row has its own point as barycenter, proving (4) by Jensen.
All sets used are Borel and the supporting slack is bounded.

The same argument, without the added diagonal law, gives for each
nonnegative convex function \(\psi\) on the facet hyperplane
\[
 \int_F\psi\,d\nu\le\int_F\psi\,d\eta.                    \tag{5}
\]
For arbitrary signed convex functions, the balanced form (4) is
the correct statement.

## 2. Exact lattice straightening and all metric factors

Let \(E:\mathbb R^{d-1}\longrightarrow u^\perp\) be a linear
isometry. For \(d=1\), its domain is the one-point vector space.
Define
\[
 \Psi(z,t)=\bigl(z,\ Et+(b-a\cdot z)u\bigr),\qquad
 D=\Psi^{-1}(F).                                        \tag{6}
\]
This is an affine bijection from \(\mathbb R^{n+d-1}\) to the
supporting hyperplane. Since \(F\) is a facet, \(D\) is a
full-dimensional compact convex polytope in that space. The map
leaves every integer base coordinate unchanged. In particular
\[
 D\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^{d-1})
   =\Psi^{-1}\bigl(F\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\bigr) \tag{7}
\]
with no rationality hypothesis on \(a,u,b\).
The base is exactly \(\operatorname{proj}_z(D)\cap\mathbb Z^n\),
so it remains lattice-complete.

At each fixed \(z=p\), (6) is an isometry in \(t\). Therefore
the pullback of the full facet restriction is exactly
\[
 \Psi^{-1}_\#(\eta|_F)
   =\mu_F:=\sum_{p\in\mathbb Z^n}
       \mathcal H_{d-1}|_{D_p},                         \tag{8}
\]
forgetting the now constant normal mark \(u\).
There is **no slope Jacobian in this mixed fiber measure**.
Indeed \(F_p\) is an exposed face of the full-dimensional
\(K_p\); it has boundary measure precisely
\(\mathcal H_{d-1}|_{F_p}\). Faces of smaller dimension have
zero such measure. Its relative interior has continuous normal
\(u\), while intersections with other own-fiber facet directions
are null. This also proves (8) at a tie between several ambient
facets inducing the same own-fiber facet. For \(d=1\), every
nonempty \(F_p\) is one endpoint and (8) is counting measure.

For clarity, the *ambient* \((n+d-1)\)-dimensional Jacobian of
\(\Psi\) is different:
\[
 J_{\rm ambient}=\sqrt{1+|a|^2}.                         \tag{9}
\]
The images of the base coordinate directions have Gram matrix
\(I_n+aa^T\), their scalar products with the images of the
\(t\)-directions vanish, and the latter Gram matrix is \(I_{d-1}\).
The first Gram matrix has eigenvalues \(1+|a|^2,1,\ldots,1\),
which proves (9). Equivalently the Jacobian of projection onto
the base, restricted to the facet tangent plane, is
\((1+|a|^2)^{-1/2}\). These two factors cancel in continuous
coarea, but (8) is a discrete fiber identity and requires
neither a base integral nor ambient facet area.

If \(\eta(F)>0\), the mixed trace of \(D\) has Hausdorff dimension
exactly \(d-1\): one of its finitely many fibers has positive
\(\mathcal H_{d-1}\)-measure. Thus the measure in (8) is also
the intrinsic Hausdorff measure of that mixed trace. A facet
with \(\eta(F)=0\) contributes no boundary transport and is
omitted, rather than assigned a different intrinsic normalization.

Pulling (4) back through the affine map gives the exact
lower-dimensional volume transport statement
\[
 \widehat\nu_F+\widehat\zeta_F\ \le_{\rm cx}\ \mu_F.       \tag{10}
\]
The hats denote the pullbacks of the two source terms in (4).
The mass of the extra term is exactly \(L_F\). Affine maps
preserve the martingale identity, so (10) includes equality
of mass and of every affine physical moment.

## 3. The exact source law and all restricted halfspaces

Suppose the source is expressed as
\[
 d\nu=\sum_j\lambda_j\alpha_j\,d\eta,\qquad \lambda_j\ge0, \tag{11}
\]
where \(\alpha_j\) are the actual bounded Borel cap allocations.
Then no additional metric factor enters its restriction:
\[
 d\widehat\nu_F=\sum_j\lambda_j
            (\alpha_j\circ\Psi)\,d\mu_F.                \tag{12}
\]

For a closed ambient cap \(H_j=\{c_j\cdot z+v_j\cdot x\ge b_j\}\)
its trace becomes exactly
\[
 \bigl(c_j-(v_j\cdot u)a\bigr)\cdot z
 +(E^Tv_j)\cdot t
 \ \ge\ b_j-(v_j\cdot u)b.                              \tag{13}
\]
Thus all oblique directions are retained. The displayed normal
may vanish, in which case the trace is the full hyperplane or
empty; otherwise it is a closed halfspace in the reduced space.
Its continuous component \(E^Tv_j\) can vanish even when the
original continuous component \(v_j\) did not.

At strict cap traces \(\alpha_j\circ\Psi\) is the indicator
of (13). On a positive-measure cap-plane coincidence, it retains
the original inside or outside branch allocation. Such a
coincidence must not be replaced by the closed indicator 1.
If all these trace boundaries have zero \(\mu_F\)-measure,
then (12) is exactly a weighted sum of their closed cap
indicators almost everywhere. No such transversality is needed
for (10)--(13).

Even when \(L_F=0\), the unweighted target in (10) is a
*volume* measure on a reduced convex body. The inherited source
is the weighted cap law (12), not a new boundary law on \(D\).
The facet restrictions of the original bulk cap budgets are
also not the same as their bulk volumes. Thus this reduction
does not recursively supply the same attained-minimum
boundary-stress hypotheses one dimension lower.

## 4. A sufficient condition for zero incoming mass

Assume \(\eta\)-almost every measured fiber-boundary point
belongs to exactly one nonvertical ambient facet. Since
\(\nu\ll\eta\), the same is true of almost every source point.
Label a point by this facet. A source row with label \(F\)
stays in \(F\) by Section 1; almost every target has a unique
label and therefore also has label \(F\). Hence the coupling
is block diagonal in these labels and
\[
 L_F=0\quad\hbox{for every nonvertical ambient facet }F.  \tag{14}
\]
Here the possible presence of vertical ambient facets is
irrelevant: they do not define a nonzero continuous own-fiber
normal. The conclusion concerns nonvertical owners only.

In this unique-ownership case, (10) has no added source term,
and its target is precisely the unweighted intrinsic
\((d-1)\)-dimensional mixed measure on the complete reduced
body (6). This is a sufficient geometric hypothesis, not
a property asserted for arbitrary lattice-complete bodies.

## 5. Positive-density obstruction on both upper facets

For every \(d\ge1\), use integer coordinate \(z\), one continuous
coordinate \(x_1\), and \(x'\in\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Put
\[
 C=\{0\le z\le4,\ -1\le x_1\le\min(z,4-z),\
                         x'\in[0,1]^{d-1}\}.            \tag{15}
\]
This is a full-dimensional compact polytope with exactly the
five integer bases \(0,1,2,3,4\). Every fiber has positive
volume, with heights \(1,2,3,2,1\).
Its two upper ambient facets are
\[
 F_L=\{x_1=z,\ 0\le z\le2,\ x'\in[0,1]^{d-1}\},
 \quad
 F_R=\{x_1=4-z,\ 2\le z\le4,\ x'\in[0,1]^{d-1}\}.         \tag{16}
\]
Their marked continuous normal is the same, \(e_1\).
At the integer base 2 they coincide along an entire
own-fiber facet of \((d-1)\)-measure 1.

Keep all other fiber-boundary components fixed by the identity
coupling. On the upper boundary assign source densities,
relative to the actual target area, as follows:
\[
 (\nu_0,\nu_1,\nu_2,\nu_3,\nu_4)
       =(3/4,\,3/2,\,1/2,\,3/2,\,3/4).                 \tag{17}
\]
For each fixed \(x'\), send source density \(3/4\) at 0 to
itself, \(1/2\) at 2 to itself, and \(3/4\) at 4 to itself.
At base 1 send densities \(1/4,1,1/4\) to bases \(0,1,2\);
at base 3 send densities \(1/4,1,1/4\) to bases \(2,3,4\).
Every target upper facet has density 1. These are physical
martingale rows: the three left upper points
\((0,0),(1,1),(2,2)\) are affine in \(z\), and the three
right upper points \((2,2),(3,1),(4,0)\) are affine in \(z\).
The weights \(1/4,1,1/4\) have the stated middle base and
height as their barycenter after division by \(3/2\).
The coordinate \(x'\) and the continuous normal never change.

Thus this is a positive-density source on the entire actual
boundary with a normal-preserving physical martingale to
the full unweighted target. Nevertheless,
\[
 \eta(F_L)=\eta(F_R)=3,\qquad
 \nu(F_L)=\nu(F_R)=\frac{11}{4},\qquad
 L_{F_L}=L_{F_R}=\frac14.                               \tag{18}
\]
The incoming target law for either facet is exactly
one quarter of the unit-area facet at base 2, supplied
from the source row on the other upper facet. Consequently
neither upper facet supports a martingale from its raw
source restriction to its full unweighted target restriction:
their masses already differ.

The reduced unweighted bodies are simply
\([0,2]\times[0,1]^{d-1}\) and
\([2,4]\times[0,1]^{d-1}\). The failure therefore occurs
despite exact lattice completeness and the simplest possible
intrinsic reduced measure. It is caused by the incoming mass,
not by irrational normals, a Jacobian, or a lower-dimensional
fiber convention. This source is not asserted to be a
minimizing critical-cap stress.

## 6. Scope of the dimension-reduction mechanism

The facet target can be identified with unweighted mixed
\((d-1)\)-measure exactly, but a raw restriction of the source
does not in general transport to all of that target. Formula
(3) measures the missing mass, and (10) gives the corrected
balanced law. Under (14), the correction vanishes.

A numerical OC implication would still have to relate these
facet volume laws and their allocations to the original
bulk cap budgets, and it would have to apply to an actual
attained source without assuming polytopal attainment.
Neither implication is supplied or presumed here.

The separate exact verifier
../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_supporting_facet_incoming_mass_coherent.py checks
all source/target masses, physical barycenters, support-plane
containments, normal preservation, both strict leaks, and
the diagonal correction in (15)--(18).
